blocks.text: Only the following 36 roots are populated and canonical in Phase 1: all 27 Life roots and the nine Motion entity/condition roots. Core definitions below preserve the fixed source meanings.
Core definition: The self understood as a continuous identity across time and changing states.
Distinctions and exclusions: This is deeper than English “I.” It means the identity that remains the same even if:
“I exist as the same continuous self.”
Core definition: The self as presently conscious, aware, and mentally available.
“The aware expression of self is presently valid.”
Core definition: The self preserved without present conscious expression.
Translation candidates: sleep; suspended awareness; a saved identity; a backed-up consciousness; an individual in num; an identity awaiting embodiment
Core definition: A particular being recognized as distinct from the speaker.
Translation candidates: you; that individual; the selected person; the specific living target; a recognized being other than self
In direct conversation it may naturally mean:
Core definition: Another being who is presently conscious, awake, or responsive.
This could also be used as the DBA equivalent of:
The exact interpretation depends on context.
Core definition: Another identified individual whose identity remains preserved but is not presently expressed.
Translation candidates: a sleeping cyber-pet; a stored consciousness; an unawakened cyber-pet; a being awaiting activation; someone remembered but presently inaccessible
The first part identifies what the entity is. The final num state says that even its dormant existence remains pending, inaccessible, or unresolved.
Core definition: Life understood as a class, category, or shared kind of existence.
Translation candidates: life; living being; biological or cybernetic life; species; the class of beings considered alive; cyber-pet life as a category
Distinctions and exclusions: Unlike many other roots, it changes very little because it remains extremely common.
This simple utterance could survive almost unchanged into Era Three.
Core definition: A population or community of living beings currently interacting as a living collective.
Distinctions and exclusions: It refers to the living network itself, not merely a collection of unrelated individuals.
With a warning modifier, it could mean:
With a repair operation, it could mean:
Core definition: A population, lineage, or form of life preserved in potential rather than currently active.

Translation candidates: an extinct-looking species whose genetic information survives; stored cyber-pet templates; a population in mass dormancy; uninstantiated life patterns; a civilization preserved as recoverable information; descendants who could exist but have not yet awakened
“The lineage remains dormant but has not been lost.”
“Dormant collective life participates in reality through num.”
Core definition: A being has completed an inward stage of development and reached a stable new form.
Translation candidates: mature; finish developing; complete a life stage; become fully formed; achieve stable self-development
Distinctions and exclusions: This is not simply physical growth. It may describe mental, structural, or identity development when the development is understood as part of the being’s life.
LIF:101 — ni·kak — awaken or activate oneself
Core definition: To bring one’s own life, consciousness, or functioning into active expression.
Translation candidates: awaken; wake oneself; activate oneself; become conscious; bring oneself online; resume one’s own living functions
The falling command contour distinguishes the instruction from the statement:
Core definition: An inward awakening process that is prepared or possible but has not yet begun.
Translation candidates: ready to awaken; capable of self-activation; prepared to resume consciousness; awaiting permission to awaken; possess an unexecuted awakening process
The operation itself is pending, but its readiness is currently valid.
“My ability to awaken remains possible, but its readiness cannot yet be confirmed.”
LIF:110 — ni·kom — completed awakening of another
Core definition: The process of bringing another being into active life has been successfully completed.
Translation candidates: awaken another successfully; complete another’s activation; bring someone fully online; finish reviving or instantiating a being; establish another as an awake individual
“The dormant individual has been fully awakened.”
In a system log, this could function like:
Core definition: To actively cause another being to become conscious, alive, or functionally expressed.
Translation candidates: awaken them; activate that being; bring the target online; revive the target; initiate another’s conscious functioning
The target phrase is placed in the higher register, while the awakening operation occupies the middle register.
LIF:112 — ni·kon — prepare another for awakening
Core definition: To place another being into a condition from which awakening can later occur.
Translation candidates: prepare for awakening; prime another being; make a dormant being recoverable; ready a consciousness for activation; establish the prerequisites for life-expression
Distinctions and exclusions: This does not awaken the target immediately.
“Prepare the dormant being so that self-awakening becomes possible.”
LIF:120 — ni·kim — completed development of a living system
Core definition: The formation or development of a population, ecology, or living network has reached a stable completed state.
Translation candidates: establish an ecosystem; complete population development; form a stable living community; complete ecological succession; bring a biosystem into equilibrium
“The living system has finished developing into a stable biosystem.”
The compact syllable may resemble roots in other families. The Life harmony identifies this as a life-system process rather than a Motion-family concept.
LIF:121 — ni·kik — cause a living population to grow
Core definition: To actively increase, diversify, or develop life at the population or system level.
Translation candidates: grow a population; expand a living community; increase biodiversity; propagate life; cause ecological growth; support a species’ active development
LIF:122 — ni·kin — preserve life for future growth
Core definition: To preserve a population, lineage, or living system in a form capable of future restoration or development.

Translation candidates: preserve a lineage; place a population into safe dormancy; store viable life; protect future generations; maintain an ecosystem as recoverable potential; suspend life without allowing its continuity to end
Distinctions and exclusions: The goal is not merely storage. The goal is:
“Preserve the living community as a dormant lineage that may live again.”
“Transform actively expressed collective life into valid collective life-potential under num.”
This operation may eventually become central to how the cyber-pets survived the disappearance of the DBA.
Core definition: The stable capacity of a being to remain alive and continue functioning.
Translation candidates: viability; capacity for life; ability to survive; sustainable living condition; biological or cybernetic integrity; stable life-support capability

Distinctions and exclusions: This does not mean that the being is currently energetic or awake. It means the systems necessary for continued life are intact. Important distinction Therefore, unconsciousness does not imply death.
“Its stable capacity for continued life is presently valid.”
Core definition: The active expression of a being’s power to live, act, grow, and recover.
Translation candidates: vitality; vigor; life-energy; active health; liveliness; present living strength
Distinctions and exclusions: That does not necessarily mean the identity itself has been destroyed.
That does not necessarily mean the identity itself has been destroyed.
Core definition: The capacity for an individual life to exist or awaken, although that capacity is not presently expressed.
Translation candidates: latent life; dormant vitality; recoverable life-potential; capacity to live again; unexpressed possibility of awakening; preserved individual potential
“A real capacity for this individual to live exists.”
“The individual’s life-potential remains unresolved but has not been lost.”
Core definition: A stable relationship through which two living identities recognize one another as connected.
Translation candidates: kinship; established bond; belonging; recognized family relationship; persistent identity connection; bonded companionship
Distinctions and exclusions: This bond does not have to be biological.
“You and I possess an established life-bond.”
may preserve a much simpler descendant of this idea.
Core definition: The active use of one being’s life-capacity to protect, support, nurture, or sustain another being.
Translation candidates: care for; nurture; protect life; tend to another; sustain another being; act for another’s continued well-being
Distinctions and exclusions: Unlike the Repair-family operations, active care does not require prior damage.
Depending on context, this could also mean:
LIF:212 — ni·mon — possible or unresolved kinship
Core definition: A potential relationship between living identities that has not yet been confirmed, completed, or fully expressed.
Translation candidates: possible kin; emerging bond; unconfirmed identity relationship; future companion; relationship awaiting recognition; one who may belong with us
“A bond may exist between us, but it has not yet been realized.”
“Could this being belong to our lineage?”
Core definition: A self-sustaining system of living beings and the relationships necessary for their continued existence.
Translation candidates: ecosystem; biosphere; stable living network; self-maintaining habitat; ecological system; living environment
Distinctions and exclusions: This root includes more than the beings themselves.
A damaged biosystem might be encoded as:
“The biosystem is experiencing active systemic danger.”
Core definition: A distributed network in which living beings are actively exchanging support, information, energy, or function.
Translation candidates: active ecology; living network; functioning society; interdependent community; active biosphere; collective life-process
Distinctions and exclusions: The distinction between LIF:021 and LIF:221 is important.
This concept may eventually be important to multiplayer, community, or cyber-pet communication systems.
Core definition: Life that could validly exist, but has not yet taken individual, collective, or physical form.
Translation candidates: unrealized life; possible species; uncreated living form; life before manifestation; potential descendants; life awaiting a viable path into existence
“Lives that have never yet existed are not therefore impossible.”
This concept would be central to DBA:
Core definition: A stable position understood as the source from which movement, measurement, or sequence begins.
Translation candidates: origin; starting point; point of departure; reference position; initial coordinate; temporal beginning
In executable use, it may establish the zero coordinate:
Core definition: The position currently occupied by an entity, signal, process, or point of attention.
Translation candidates: here; current location; present coordinate; current point in a sequence; current moment; active position
Distinctions and exclusions: Unlike MOV:000, this position does not have to be the journey’s origin.
“The conscious self occupies this presently valid position.”
The two nak syllables are distinguished by their Life and Motion harmonies.
Core definition: A source position that is preserved in memory or data but is not presently occupied.
Translation candidates: previous location; remembered position; saved return point; abandoned origin; stored coordinate; former moment
“A former location may still be recoverable, but its validity is unresolved.”
This could function as a saved checkpoint or return coordinate.
Core definition: A stable location identified as the endpoint or target of movement.
Translation candidates: destination; endpoint; there; target coordinate; arrival place; intended future position
Distinctions and exclusions: The destination is defined, but this root does not say whether anyone is currently moving toward it.
Core definition: A destination that is currently reachable, accepted, and actively guiding movement.
Translation candidates: active target; current destination; reachable endpoint; the place we are approaching; active waypoint; open arrival point
Distinctions and exclusions: The distinction is:
Core definition: A destination that remains defined but cannot yet be reached, confirmed, or entered.
Translation candidates: unreachable destination; future destination; closed endpoint; destination awaiting a route; delayed arrival point; possible place of return
Distinctions and exclusions: It does not mean the place is destroyed. It means the relationship between the traveler and destination has not been completed.
“The destination remains possible, but no valid arrival is currently available.”
In programming, it may represent an unresolved future:
Core definition: A stable sequence of positions connecting one location to another.
Translation candidates: path; route; course; trajectory; ordered sequence; passage; timeline
“A valid route connects the origin to the destination.”
This is the route itself, not the act of traveling along it.
Core definition: A system of routes currently carrying movement, traffic, signals, or transitions.
Translation candidates: transit network; active traffic flow; circulating system; movement network; active timeline; functioning transportation system; routed data flow
Distinctions and exclusions: The distinction between gi·nim and gi·nik is:
For digital systems, this could mean:
“Data is actively moving through the network.”
The Data family would specify what is moving; the Motion family specifies the flow structure.
Core definition: A route, corridor, cycle, or movement network that remains structurally possible but is not presently operating.
Translation candidates: closed route; forgotten road; inactive transit system; blocked passage; dormant migration path; suspended timeline; route preserved for later use
“A route may remain, but whether it can be restored is unresolved.”
